item.title: Version 1.0.0
item.description:
# Battery Sensei 1.0
The first public release of Battery Sensei — a quiet macOS menu-bar utility that watches your battery, learns the shape of your day, and nudges you to plug in before the bottom falls out.
## What's inside
- **Warnings that match your tone.** Three calm presets — gentle Info banner, persistent Warning badge, full-screen Alert kamehameha — plus a Custom tier where every threshold, dismissal mode, and auto-close timing is yours. - **Meeting Battery Guard.** Optional read-only calendar access. Sensei projects your charge against the next four hours of meetings and tells you exactly when to plug in. Pick which checkpoints fire (`−30 min`, `−15 min`, `−5 min`, `−1 min`) with the on-device chip toggles. Default `−30` + `−5` gives you an early heads-up and a last-chance ping. - **Today.** Live capacity, cycle count, time-since-plug-in, and a soft history strip so you can see what your battery has been through this week at a glance. - **Sensei Saga.** Per-app battery share over the last 1 h / 24 h / 7 d, ranked. Tap a row for a chart and detail card. Search to drill in. - **Charge cap recommendations.** Daily ceiling with weekly full-cycle reminders so the gauge stays honest. - **Auto-update via Sparkle.** Signed EdDSA + Apple-notarized PKGs delivered straight from `battery-sensei.app`.
## Languages
English, Deutsch, Español, Français, 日本語 — fully localized including notifications, share cards, calendar alerts, and accessibility labels.
## Requires
- macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later - Apple Silicon or Intel - Calendar access is optional and read-only
Drag the installer into Applications and Sensei takes it from there.
ありがとうございます。

item.title: Version 1.1.0
item.description:
# Battery Sensei 1.1
A polish-and-precision release for Meeting Battery Guard, the warnings UI, and the auto-update plumbing. If you're on 1.0, Sparkle will offer you this build the next time you launch the app.
## Highlights
### Meeting Battery Guard — redesigned reminder system
The single "max two fires per meeting" rule has been replaced with a **multi-checkpoint system** that mirrors the website's `REMINDS YOU AT −30 −15 −5 −1` strip. Toggle which checkpoints fire — Sensei sends exactly one notification per enabled checkpoint, per meeting.
- **Default checkpoints**: `−30 min` (early heads-up) and `−1 min` plus `−5 min` available, all chips in a dashed-border row inside the meeting guard settings. - **Visual emphasis** on the final chip (`−1 min`) when selected — matches the warning tint the website uses to mark the last reminder. - **Always-visible Latest forecast** card. When no meeting needs attention, the section shows a calm "No conflicts" empty state with the lookahead window. The Preview button stays in reach in both states. - **Live countdown** — the "Happening now · N min left" / "Starts in X min" strip now redraws on a 30-second wall-clock schedule, independent of Combine state updates, so the minute counter actually counts down. - **`Forecast.event.titleRedacted` updates the moment you flip "Show event titles"** — previously the title cached at forecast time and stayed stale until the next refresh. - **OSLog instrumentation** — every fire (or suppression) logs to Console.app under `subsystem:io.schaier.battery-sensei category:calendar.notifier` so you can verify the cadence in real time.
### Overlay polish — meeting alerts look different from battery warnings
Meeting overlays now use a dedicated layout: - Calendar icon (`calendar.badge.exclamationmark`) instead of the battery glyph. - Prediction sentence ("Your laptop dies 17 min into standup. Plug in now.") promoted to **serif display** typography as the hero. - Percentage readout and drain bar suppressed — the message is the message. - Small uppercase tracked kicker ("Meeting battery guard") anchors the context.
All three notification styles (Info / Warning / Alert) carry these changes; the alert tint differentiates urgency.
### Hover affordances — the small things
Audited every custom button in the app for hover state. Three buttons that had no visible affordance now scale + brighten on pointer-over with `prefers-reduced-motion` respected:
- Snooze title button in the warning overlay - Snooze `−` / `+` step buttons (disabled state honoured — no scale lift when the button is unavailable) - Reminder chips in Meeting Battery Guard (border thickens + scale lifts; pointing-hand cursor on entry)
### Settings window — proper Mac app, not a popover
The Settings window now owns the app's activation policy. When Settings is open, Battery Sensei behaves like a regular Mac app: Dock icon visible, Cmd-Tab targetable, and windows stay anchored when you click another app. When Settings closes, the app drops back to its menu-bar-only state. **Calendar permission prompts and other system dialogs no longer make the Settings window vanish.**
- Removed the zoom + miniaturize traffic-light buttons — Settings is a sized, single-purpose surface, not a free-floating document window.
### Reminder fires, audited
Notifications are now strictly `(eventID, checkpoint)`-deduped. No severity escalation between checkpoints can sneak in a third fire; downgrades never re-emit. The OSLog stream lets you verify this in real time.
## Bug fixes
- **EventKit prompt + accessory policy**: clicking "Allow Full Access" no longer closes the Settings window. The fix lives at the window layer instead of the per-call workaround that shipped in 1.0. - **Lookahead persistence**: removed the user-facing Lookahead control. The fixed 4-hour scan window applies for everyone; reminders cap how many notifications fire so the extra knob added no signal. Any previously-persisted custom value (8h, 12h) collapses to 4h on next launch. - **Show / Hide event titles toggle inversion**: the toggle now reads positively ("Show event titles in notifications"). Defaults to on, with a one-time migration that resets the old "Hide" preference so users who previously enabled redaction can opt back in deliberately under the new framing.
## Requires
- macOS 14 (Sonoma) or later - Apple Silicon or Intel
Drag the installer into Applications and Sensei takes it from there.
ありがとうございます。
